prompt.en: A newly coordinated repeater has a published channel pair, but users still cannot bring it up unless their radios send the required access tone. Which explanation combines both facts?

text.en: Coordination helps reduce channel conflicts; the programmed transmit CTCSS tone is still needed to open that receiver.
Coordination automatically inserts the access tone into every user radio in the coverage area.
A CTCSS tone replaces frequency coordination, so the repeater channel pair no longer matters.
The access tone changes the repeater into simplex operation whenever the channel is busy.

explanation.en: Coordination and CTCSS solve different problems. Coordination plans repeater channels; the access tone is a receiver-opening condition for users.

prompt.en: Which statement is NOT true about repeater access and shared-channel courtesy?

text.en: A required transmit CTCSS tone must be sent by your radio for the repeater receiver to open correctly.
A time-out timer is a backstop for excessive transmissions, not permission to hold the channel until it stops you.
A fallback plan helps when two stations try simplex and the direct channel is unusable.
If you hear the repeater output strongly, the transmit offset and transmit tone can no longer affect whether others hear you.

explanation.en: Receiving the repeater output does not prove your transmitted signal is set up correctly. The offset and transmit access tone still matter on the input side.

prompt.en: A 20-metre voice operator is set to lower sideband and hears an existing contact only about 2 kHz away. Which combined correction fits the lesson?

text.en: Use the 20-metre upper-sideband convention and choose a spot with about 3 kHz or more from the contact.
Keep lower sideband because moving closer than 3 kHz makes the wrong sideband easier to copy.
Stay 2 kHz away if the other station is weak, because sideband convention replaces spacing courtesy.
Switch to a repeater offset, because offset programming provides SSB separation on HF.

explanation.en: The operator must satisfy both ideas: use the expected 20-metre sideband and leave enough SSB spacing from the contact already in progress.
